context: Prashant deposits money into a bank account that pays simple interest. Amounts are in rands (R). The final amount is the capital plus all the interest earned.
stem: Prashant deposits $\text{R}{=p}$ into a bank account that pays a simple interest rate of ${=r}$ % p.a. How many years must he leave the money in the account for it to grow to $\text{R}{=a}$ ?
solution: Read the question carefully and write down the given information: $\begin{aligned}A&=\text{R}{=a}\\P&=\text{R}{=p}\\i&=\frac{{=r}}{100}={=i}\\n&=?\end{aligned}$
To calculate the number of years, we need to make $n$ the subject of the formula: $\begin{aligned}A&=P(1+in)\\\frac{A}{P}&=1+in\\\frac{A}{P}-1&=in\\\frac{\frac{A}{P}-1}{i}&=n\end{aligned}$
It will take ${=n}$ years for $\text{R}{=p}$ to grow to $\text{R}{=a}$ at a simple interest rate of ${=r}$ % p.a.
notes: Basic tier: the entry point of the skill. Every instance is built forwards from a whole number of years n, so A = P(1 + in) holds exactly and the answer is a whole number with no rounding. P is a multiple of R500 (R1000 to R20000) so the interest per year is a whole number of rands and A is a whole number. The rate is a whole percentage chosen from a list that skips 10, so i always prints with exactly two decimals (0.04 to 0.15) and never with a trailing zero. The solution follows the book's own skeleton (write down A, P, i, n; make n the subject; substitute; state the answer) from worked example 3 on p.333. The book's round-up-to-the-nearest-year rule is deliberately left to the standard and advanced book questions, so the two catalogued rounding misconceptions (rounds-n-to-nearest-not-up, rounds-too-early) do not apply here and no distractors are needed (numeric, not mcq). Check one instance: k=6, r=8, n=5 gives P=3000, A=4200, i=0.08, n=(4200/3000-1)/0.08=5.
